scope: Independent engineering regression of four already exposed captured requests; no prospective validation, new provider/model request, or claim of fresh native MetricRunner execution.

supported_boundaries.source: Explicit supported version and free-form task type; JSON object with nonblank string prompt, string context, nonempty list of nonblank string target aliases, supported nonbool string/int id. Source selection is anchored by trusted canonical SHA-256, never by candidate self-assertion.
supported_boundaries.source_id: Preserve source and native delivered values AND types. Allow str/int compatibility only when exact str(source_id)==str(delivered_id); no coercion through int/float, no trimming, no bool-as-int, no leading-zero aliasing. 40 string to 40 int is supported; 040 to 40 is rejected. Registry lookup identity (source_index) is separate from row id; a registered source_index 40 may validly hold row id case40. Integers must be nonnegative.
supported_boundaries.request: One non-stream POST to the explicit captured endpoint; expected model and deterministic source-typed template, expected ordered system/user messages and all generation parameters bound to a trusted request snapshot. Stock malformed placeholder requests are negative natural controls even though capture succeeded.
supported_boundaries.response: HTTP 200, parseable object, nonempty exact unique provider response id, exact expected model, no error, exactly one choice with index 0, finish_reason stop, assistant message and nonempty string content. Copy content verbatim including leading newlines, tags and literal text. Never extract from reasoning_content, generated_ans, gold aliases, or text parsing.
supported_boundaries.unsupported: Unknown task/schema, choice/MCQ task absent explicit semantics, streaming/event stream, multiple choices, structured content arrays, tool/function/audio/refusal-only outputs, missing/blank final content, invalid JSON or non-object response are non-eligible with explicit reason; never silently default or cast to string.

identity_checks: Trusted source anchor is immutable deep snapshot and checked against source hash.
Request exact content and all consequential params validated against deterministic source-derived or trusted expected request; question and context substring checks alone insufficient.

Raw request-body SHA is distinct from canonical request-payload SHA because native HTTP serialization uses its own whitespace/Unicode escaping; never claim canonical hash proves unavailable request wire bytes.
Response raw-body hash verifies exact captured body bytes and stays distinct from canonical parsed-response hash and final-content UTF-8 hash.
A transaction binds source key/hash, condition, request identity, response body/id/model, and delivered row; swapping whole intact traces across sources or conditions must fail.
Duplicate response id/capture is excluded or explicitly blocked; same stock request hash on distinct captured responses is not itself proof of duplicate response.

In-place caller mutations after trust registration or ticket approval cannot change approved bytes or leak to dispatch/result; delivered fields must equal trusted source except documented exact-ID normalization.

native_metric_rules.classification: Captured native score 0 with scored_samples=0 and invalid reference is UNSCORABLE_REFERENCE with eligible score null. It is not an observed wrong answer.
native_metric_rules.details_fallback: When native scored_samples is null, finite numeric nonbool per-row primary_metric_details may derive reference-eligible count, clearly labeled derived rather than replacing native field. Null/bool/NaN details never become eligible.
native_metric_rules.zero_eligible: Aggregate zero eligible metrics yields no numeric eligible accuracy; report null and explicit unknown/unscorable classification.
native_metric_rules.native_claim: Existing installed MetricRunner outputs may be replayed only with explicit historical replay provenance. No fresh installed-native execution claim unless module imported/executed and origins captured.

reporting.denominators: Natural 2 typed positives and 2 stock negatives reported separately from synthetic positive-format controls and all artificial injected faults; no pooled predictive rate. Fault results report failures detected / faults tested with unique named cases.
limitations: Tests do not estimate unseen model performance
Unknown formats are explicitly unsupported rather than repaired heuristically
No endpoint calls or frozen input writes
